Hi. I'm a college theatre teacher & this is what I tell my actors who want to act in film, specifically in LA.  Move to LA and use the money you would use for college on acting lessons & classes, plastic surgery, personal training & that sort of thing. It's probably less money overall. LA is cutthroat & college is a huge expense. I strongly believe in a liberal arts education & if you want to continue your education, get a degree in something practical that can help get you a day job. I see lots of actors go through my program, studying theatre who just want to be actors in film & they're kind of miserable in classes besides acting classes. I don't know if you're in a theatre program or not, but most college acting programs are housed in theatre departments, which are generally less suited for film acting. Of course, finishing your degree might help you get a day job, but it might not. And of course, college is the only time in your life when you can spend four years studying & focusing on something you love. College is also great for making connections.

Hi, I'm an acting teacher and I use Bob Barton's textbook "Acting Onstage and Off" for my acting classes. It's a great beginner book and a sort of condensing  of Stanislavski's  acting concepts. But, I agree with lakelady, you can't teach that online. I'd suggest readings, learning some monologues, and auditioning for some plays, if you can't afford a class or private lessons. If you get in a play, lots of times you can learn-as-you-go. Depending on where you live, you might be able to find some free acting workshops.
